<STRUCT_0001>
Here are some common types of separation conditions, relative to the base
scheme <MATH_0001>. There is also an absolute notion of these conditions which we
will discuss in
Properties of Spaces, Section <REF_0001>.
Moreover, we will discuss separation conditions for a morphism of
algebraic spaces in
Morphisms of Spaces, Section <REF_0002>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme contained in <MATH_0002>.
Let <MATH_0003> be an algebraic space over <MATH_0004>.
Let <MATH_0005> be the diagonal morphism.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> We say <MATH_0006> is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>separated over <MATH_0007><TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if <MATH_0008> is a closed immersion.
<STRUCT_0003> We say <MATH_0009> is <TEXTITOPEN_0002>locally separated over <MATH_0010><TEXTITCLOSE_0002><FOOTNOTEOPEN_0001>In the
literature this often refers to quasi-separated and
locally separated algebraic spaces.<FOOTNOTECLOSE_0001> if <MATH_0011> is an
immersion.
<STRUCT_0004> We say <MATH_0012> is <TEXTITOPEN_0003>quasi-separated over <MATH_0013><TEXTITCLOSE_0003> if <MATH_0014> is quasi-compact.
<STRUCT_0005> We say <MATH_0015> is <TEXTITOPEN_0004>Zariski locally quasi-separated over <MATH_0016><TEXTITCLOSE_0004><FOOTNOTEOPEN_0002>This
definition was suggested by B.<SPACE_0001>Conrad.<FOOTNOTECLOSE_0002> if there
exists a Zariski covering <MATH_0017> such that
each <MATH_0018> is quasi-separated.
<STRUCT_0006>

<STRUCT_0001>
Note that if the diagonal is quasi-compact (when <MATH_0001> is separated or
quasi-separated) then the diagonal is actually
quasi-finite and separated, hence quasi-affine (by More on Morphisms,
Lemma <REF_0001>).
